title: Convergence of the KMP model to the KPZ equation: the limiting constant of the scaling (Proposition 6.7)
author: Guillaume Barraquand, Francesco Casini
work: Convergence of the KMP model to the KPZ equation
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the proposition printed as Proposition 6.7 of "Convergence of the KMP model to the KPZ equation" (source0.tex lines 1107--1112, source label proposition-limitingConstant), delivered with the article's own complete proof at source0.tex lines 1113--1270 (158 lines, one adjacent proof environment). It computes the limit of the scaling constant gamma_epsilon squared and obtains 1/(2 alpha), which is the constant entering the KPZ equation obtained as the scaling limit of the KMP process; it is the last ingredient of the article's proof of its main convergence theorem. The proof is complete inside the retained span and is not a routine exercise: it rewrites the numerator as a covariance of the quenched displacements of two walkers that can be correlated only through a common Bernoulli event, expands the covariance along the telescopic identity, uses the invariance of the re-normalized invariant measure of the Beta random walk in random environment, treats the remaining cases z in {-1,0,1} separately with the local transition probabilities, and then computes the denominator and takes the limit. Rated H2 because it is a substantial research-level computation inside a KPZ/RWRE paper, requiring the two-walker covariance calculus, the invariant-measure normalisation and a case analysis over the environment, but it is a technical computation that the paper itself presents as the final step of a longer strategy rather than the strategy's flagship theorem.
